claims.claim: Someone who has got married or formed a civil partnership and has a marriage or civil partnership certificate can use it to change the name on their licence.
claims.quote: your marriage or civil partnership certificate (if you’ve changed your surname)
claims.note: The text lists a marriage or civil partnership certificate as evidence of a name change for a driving licence application.

claims.claim: The service is for when the name on your current driving licence needs changing.
claims.quote: Change the name, title or gender on your driving licence by completing form D1 and sending it with your licence and supporting documents to DVLA.
claims.note: The guide covers changing the name on an existing driving licence.

claims.claim: Driving licence holders who change their name are legally required to update their licence to their current legal name.
claims.note: The text explains how to change the name on a licence but never says doing so is a legal requirement; the only 'must' about name changes concerns the V5C log book.

claims.claim: The service covers name changes after marriage or civil partnership.
claims.quote: your marriage or civil partnership certificate (if you’ve changed your surname)
claims.note: Marriage or civil partnership certificates are accepted as proof of a changed name.

claims.claim: The service covers name changes made by deed poll or statutory declaration.
claims.quote: If you’re using a deed poll or statutory declaration You must also send one document showing your new name.
claims.note: Deed polls and statutory declarations are accepted as proof of a name change.

claims.claim: The service is for driving licence holders who have changed their name.
claims.quote: Send DVLA your old driving licence along with the right application form and any supporting documents to change your name or gender.
claims.note: The service is for existing licence holders changing their name.
